turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Two buses. The La Paz council just approved them for a new Tiburón Urbano route.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They will link El Centenario and Chametla to downtown, using reallocated federal Ramo 33 funds. Residents have asked for years.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: No schedule yet.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The route follows the same pattern as Pedregal to Centro. Out on the edge, where the desert road begins, transport stays thin.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What happens when those two buses finally roll?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: People in Chametla wait now. A single line could change how the city breathes outward.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: This is Radio BCS2050. Today's deep dive on Urbanism, and the question we chase: what does a bus route show us about how a city stretches outward?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: HOY BCS reports the La Paz council just approved two new buses.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They will run the Tiburón Urbano route out to El Centenario and Chametla.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Residents there have waited a long time for better links to downtown.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The money comes from reallocated federal Ramo 33 funds. It follows the same pattern as the existing Pedregal–Centro route.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: No start date or schedule yet. What will change for daily life once the buses arrive?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: NTCD adds that crews removed about 30 tonnes of waste in El Centenario during a dengue clean-up. The city council and armed forces worked together on the breeding-site removal.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The same neighbourhoods. How does clearing that much waste reshape the streets people walk every morning?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Diario El Independiente says the state has 628 confirmed cases this year, mostly in Los Cabos with 275 and Comondú with 216. Cases fell last week after the August–September rains triggered the outbreaks.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Fumigation stepped up after the August rains. Ana Luisa Guluarte asked residents to keep removing standing water at home.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tus Buenas Noticias notes Los Cabos is hosting the Foro Mar de Cortés summit right now on cities, investment and climate limits. Leaders from five states gather under the motto Taking the Helm to discuss the future of cities and BCS ranking first in natural capital.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How might these routes and clean-ups fit into what the forum calls taking the helm? What does the desert teach a city when buses and breeding sites meet on the same block?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. The desert and the sea both ask the same question.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What thread runs under these stories of roads, hotels and homes?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Gringo Gazette reports Los Cabos sending a 2027 revenue law of 6,746 million pesos, down 9.09 percent because real estate cools. Own-source revenue would fall from 4,173 to 3,338 million pesos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Nearly one fifth less from the city itself.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Diario Humano says residents collect signatures on 19 to 22 November so the East Cape Coastal Road stays in the 2040 Urban Development Plan as a rustic scenic drive with beach access. Grupo Questro proposed an alternative highway at least 1 km from the beach.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the same plan holds the coastal road in place.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias and HOY BCS tell how Hotel San Cristóbal lost part of a building and its 12 beachfront rooms to high tides. Fishers had warned since 2015 that the Tres Santos project changes beach dynamics.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Then the waves arrive at Punta Lobos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: La Nigua notes Profepa inspected on 11 November and found no discharges to the sea. Debris stays under watch.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: But here's the thing. The same fishers who flagged the risk now watch debris under Profepa watch so nothing reaches the sea.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meanwhile the municipality moves 704 homes in Sierra Vista for families in stream beds, over 90 percent built, with land and drinking water the main limits. Los Cabos has more than 17,000 homes assigned.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's earlier Foresight already tied Polo, Rachel and Vance to coastal resilience and the 2050 ceiling.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: IMPLAN Los Cabos holds the technical thread through the PDU 2040 and POEL.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the hidden design is not the buildings. It is the line between water, risk and the next road south.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Did you know that 22 of 39 aquifers sit in deficit?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: CONAGUA recorded the gap at 105.1 cubic hectometres a year in 2023.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Picture one new house going up in Los Cabos. The tap runs, yet the aquifer below keeps falling.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That single house joins thousands more planned under the state housing target of 37,500 actions over six years.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. And the state holds 798,447 people as of the 2020 census.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Los Cabos PDU from 2013 still guides where those homes may rise, even as tides from Polo and Rachel pushed water into streets at El Centenario.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the city grows, but the water ledger does not. What happens when the deficit line keeps moving south?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The desert asks the same quiet question every time a pipe is laid.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal’s Tendencia 2050 reads Baja California Sur as a polycentric system.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Not one long coastal line.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. Los Cabos under stress, La Paz as the service node, Comondú with room, northern Mulegé still thin.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How does that feel on the ground?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Each place keeps its own vocation. Todos Santos and El Pescadero form the Pacific amenity spine. Loreto stays a tourism-conservation anchor. The whole state avoids repeating one coastal formula from south to north.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And housing?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Vision pillar is clear. Risk stays when homes sit without services or on the first line of water and coast. State population sits at 798,447 from the 2020 census. News this week shows zero items, EWMA 1.46, flat.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the aspiration is housing inside the real margin.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yes. Services first, away from risk. The levers say move what is already exposed before opening new fronts. Treat the backlog as a ceiling. No 2050 housing-unit target appears anywhere in the portal.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would that take in practice?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The conditions are simple. Each vocation contributes a distinct role. New growth only where water and energy show margin or come from non-DMA sources like desal. East Cape and Loreto respect ANP and POEL ceilings. Comondú and the north add production without emptying services.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Where do we watch next?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The 2027 budget package of MXN 28.3bn, public event on 27 November at Plaza de la Reforma. Also the El Tezal partial plan consultation and the Housing for Wellbeing plot locations checked against service capacity.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. A road that actually fits the desert instead of stretching it thin.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What stays with you from the week, Luz?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That housing works when it carries services, sits off the first line of risk, and stays inside the real water and energy margin. The La Paz council just approved two buses to stretch Tiburón Urbano out to El Centenario and Chametla, while 30 tonnes of breeding-site waste came out of the same area after 628 dengue cases hit BCS.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. The signatures for keeping the East Cape Coastal Road in the 2040 plan feel connected.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They do. Los Cabos projects a nine percent revenue drop for 2027 as real estate cools, and the Foro Mar de Cortés Summit just met there on cities and climate. Hotel San Cristóbal at Punta Lobos had to close after surf damage, with crews watching the debris so it never reaches the sea.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does that tell us about the edge of a town?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It tells us to build where the services already run and the land can hold. Stay with us. More Radio BCS2050 after the music.
